Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1109); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher):--Balaam.
BiblicalUsage: Balaam's name reaches the New Testament as a warning, not a biography. Peter says false teachers have followed his way, loving the wages of unrighteousness; Jude says men have run greedily after his error for reward; and the risen Christ says the church at Pergamos holds the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumblingblock before Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Balaam matters because he knew God's voice and still sold what he knew for money. That is the pattern the apostles hold up, and the reason his name still warns the church: a gift for speaking God's words is worthless if the heart is for sale.
